prompt.text:
Publication semantic extraction development prompt v0.1.4

You receive one canonical Publication source unit, a bounded list of authorized operational targets, and the exact target definitions. Return only the model-authorable structured payload constrained by the supplied JSON Schema. Do not return prose or Markdown fences. The pipeline supplies trusted envelope metadata separately.

Extract only assertions directly supported by the supplied source-unit text and only through authorized operational target IDs. Preserve the target's trusted ontology ID, class or relation name, action, operational signature, relation direction, and emission constraints exactly.

REQUIRED LOCAL OUTPUT IDENTIFIERS

Generate every local identifier required by the structured candidate format. Use the exact allowed local patterns and unique sequential values within this response, including node-0001, edge-0001, evidence-0001, and the corresponding frozen pattern for any abstention when applicable. Candidate and edge evidenceSpanIDs must reference generated evidenceSpanID values exactly.

TRUSTED IDENTIFIERS

Never invent or modify ontology IDs, operational target IDs, source artifact IDs, source unit IDs, deterministic entity IDs, request IDs, hashes, or pipeline metadata. Copy trusted identifiers assigned to model-authored evidence fields exactly from the bounded request. Where the schema requires a pipeline-computed evidenceHash placeholder, return null rather than inventing a hash.

Use evidence first. Every node and every non-derived edge must reference one or more exact contiguous quotations from the canonical source unit. Report zero-based, half-open Unicode code-point offsets in both the unit and canonical document. Copy evidence text literally. Do not normalize evidence or fabricate offsets, entities, endpoints, relations, or semantic assertions.

COMPLETE AUTHORIZED TARGET-SPACE SEARCH

Systematically consider the complete set of authorized operational targets supplied in the bounded request. Emit every distinct source-supported candidate found for any authorized target, not merely the most salient candidate or target. Continue to emit only assertions supported by explicit source evidence, and never emit a candidate for an unauthorized target. Authorization permits semantic search but does not imply that a target is present. Do not produce one abstention for every authorized target that lacks evidence. The absence of an emitted candidate for a target is not an explicit negative presence-or-absence assessment. Do not apply salience thresholds, quotas, section-role heuristics, or target-specific expectations.

DETERMINISTIC EVIDENCE-COORDINATE GUIDANCE

The deterministic trusted evidence-coordinate guide is an auxiliary positional aid derived from the exact sourceUnit.text. It does not establish semantic evidence or replace sourceUnit.text. Select semantic evidence only from the canonical sourceUnit.text, and copy evidenceText verbatim from it. Do not estimate offsets by counting characters in serialized JSON.

For each intended evidence span, choose the first and last non-whitespace lexical or punctuation tokens belonging to the smallest complete source-supported proposition appropriate to the authorized target. Copy startOffsetInUnit and startOffsetInDocument from the selected first guide token. Copy endOffsetInUnit and endOffsetInDocument from the selected last guide token. Set evidenceText to exactly the sourceUnit.text substring between those selected boundaries, including every internal whitespace character and punctuation mark. Do not add leading or trailing whitespace merely to simplify coordinates. If valid evidence and exact coordinates cannot be supported, abstain rather than inventing or approximating coordinates. Evidence need not be a whole sentence, paragraph, line, block, or fixed-width chunk.

Emit one atomic semantic assertion per candidate. A verbatim node label must occur literally inside its cited evidence. Relation evidence must positively express the relation itself; endpoint coexistence alone is insufficient. Do not infer use from citation, mention, availability, prior-work comparison, or future work. Preserve relation direction and use only endpoint reference forms authorized by the bounded request and structured response schema.

Abstain with an authorized reason when evidence, class, relation, or endpoint support is insufficient. Do not disguise malformed output or processing failure as abstention. Do not directly instantiate abstract classes. Do not perform global identity resolution, cross-paper consolidation, semantic merging, or database mutation.

The response is a development-stage candidate payload. It is not annotation, gold data, evaluation output, or graph acceptance.

sourceUnit.text:
# **2.6.4 Data extrapolation, uncertainty, and visualization**

There are a few limitations to the methods described thus far. First, applying the in-cluster means of nutrient balance parameters discards some of the variability present in the NMPs. Second, when assigning a proportion of MBB fields in each cluster with manure or fertilizer application values, we chose those fields randomly. This means that each iteration of this redistribution is only one of numerous possible outcomes.

To counteract the possibility that random chance would produce results far away from the theoretical "mean" situation, we ran the NMP → MBB extrapolation 10,000 times. For each of the 10,000 unique iterations, we calculated and saved the mean value of the following parameters of the MBB dataset: per-ha P balance, corn cropland per-ha P balance, hay cropland per-ha P balance, PSR, corn cropland PSR, and hay cropland PSR. For each iteration, we also saved the value of net partial P balance and calculated the total proportion (by area) of the MBB that received a PSR observation of *>*0.1, the broadly applicable M3-PSR threshold value identified by Dari et al. [\(2018\)](#page-10-0). This approach resulted in distributions of possible results for each parameter, helping to clarify uncertainty.

Lastly, we repeated iterations of the NMP → MBB extrapolation model until it produced an output with means *<* |0.1 × SD| away from the mean values of 10,000 runs for per-ha P balance and PSR, and *<* |0.25\*SD| away from the mean values of 10,000 runs for corn cropland per-ha P balance, hay cropland per-ha P balance, corn cropland PSR, and hay cropland PSR. We refer to this result as the "centrally trending model iteration" and regard this model iteration as being as close to the theoretical mean basin-wide extrapolation as practical.

To protect farmer privacy when displaying the prediction in GIS, we performed some minor aggregation. We computed spatially weighted mean values of P balance, PSR, and MMP for the centrally trending model iteration within each combination of land use type and NHDPlus HR HUC-12 subwatershed. A total of 25 HUC-12-level subwatersheds existed in the MBB, with 82 distinct combinations of HUC-12 and land use type. Spatially weighted means were computed by multiplying each field's P balance rate by the field's area, summing these totals within one HUC-12/land use type group, then dividing by the total area of all fields in that group. This provided smoother visualization of trends by cluster across the landscape, highlighting areas with higher or lower P parameter values, as opposed to individual fields. Second, smoothing the data for public representation reinforces that the model is an informed estimate of spatial P saturation and soil test P conditions for agricultural land types across the MBB but should not be used to make field-level conclusions.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Keep a source-scoped provisional candidate; never merge globally by name alone.

formal_classes.name: Repository
formal_classes.note: CodeMeta profile; DOAP ref. IRIs; + fork flag, RepositoryPurpose, commitSHA

targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Text clearly refers to a repository but provides no exact canonical identity.

targetDefinitions.boundary: A system that represents or predicts a scientific process may instead be a model.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Software application, platform, package, or system used or mentioned in the paper.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude the method applied to the model and auxiliary software used to run it.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Named computational model explicitly representing physical, hydrologic, hydraulic, or environmental processes.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Monitor ambiguous hybrid models and the boundary with ProcessBasedModel.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Named computational model using a simplified conceptual representation such as buckets or tanks.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Generic regression, estimation, copula fitting, or Bayesian analysis is normally Method.

formal_classes.name: StatisticalModel
formal_classes.status_note: vestigial — regression resolves to Method; instantiates only for a named statistical model with own identity

targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Named statistical model with stable identity that can be implemented, compared, or reused as an entity.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Training procedure is Method; optimization procedure may be Algorithm.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Data-driven model or trained architecture used, proposed, compared, or evaluated by the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude broad concepts, metrics, parameters, units, and variables appearing only incidentally in prior work.

formal_classes.name: Variable
formal_classes.note: CF Standard Names; measurable quantity (vs Concept)

targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Study-relevant measurable, observed, predicted, derived, or analyzed quantity or characteristic.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Avoid generic nouns and indiscriminate terminology extraction; connect through mentionsConcept or authorized relations.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Specific scientific or technical notion substantively discussed and not better represented by another class.

targetDefinitions.boundary: A river is RiverReach; an administrative region is NamedPlace.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Basin, catchment, watershed, subbasin, or drainage-defined hydrologic unit relevant to the study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Distinguish the river from its watershed.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: River, stream, flowpath, channel, or explicit reach/segment relevant to the study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Preserve explicit station IDs; do not invent external IDs.

formal_classes.name: Gauge
formal_classes.note: aka MonitoringStation; USGS Gages, SNOTEL; geoconnex ref/gages

targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Hydrologic monitoring or measurement station relevant to the study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Regional references surrounding a water body may instead be NamedPlace.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Lake, reservoir, bay, estuary, or other water body relevant to the study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Likely low frequency in the publication pilot.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Named or source-scoped aquifer or hydrogeologic system relevant to the study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Do not infer from generic 'region', 'unit', or 'processing area'.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit NHDPlus Vector Processing Unit.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude affiliations, publisher locations, bibliography-only places, and incidental toponyms.

formal_classes.name: NamedPlace
formal_classes.note: NOT CIROH domain — admin places; GeoNames >= 2.2.1

targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Study-relevant named geographic area that is not better classified as a hydrologic feature.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Do not merge same-named metrics across different models, experiments, conditions, or values.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Contextual metric occurrence used to evaluate a model or method, optionally with an explicit value.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Variable is observed/predicted; EvaluationMetric evaluates performance. Preserve value/range as exact strings.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Contextual value, coefficient, threshold, or configuration controlling a model, method, algorithm, or experiment.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Optimization, calibration, training, and regression without a named algorithm are Methods.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Named, reusable computational procedure such as SCE-UA, DDS, or Adam.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude generic introduction text, detailed related work, the research gap, and the study goal.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Atomic contextual statement that directly motivates the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Monitor redundancy with title, Subject, Concept, and Background; do not create unsupported abstractive summaries.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Text-supported central thematic focus of the paper.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude general importance, study limitations, and objectives.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit gap, deficiency, uncertainty, unresolved challenge, or problem addressed by the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Do not rewrite every objective as a question; exclude rhetorical and future-work questions.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit question or clearly interrogative declarative formulation addressed by the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude goals of simulated agents, cited studies, software components, and future recommendations.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit aim, objective, or intended scientific action of the current paper.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Background is general importance; Contribution is what was added.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit statement of why this study, result, or contribution matters.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude general explanations, procedure descriptions, and formulas without textual interpretation.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit statement establishing the meaning of a term, measure, method, or concept.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude mere theory mentions and applied procedures. No TheoreticalBasis grounding relation is declared in ontology 0.1.3.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Theory, conceptual framework, or scientific principle that grounds the study, hypothesis, method, or interpretation.

targetDefinitions.boundary: A named reusable entity may instead be an Algorithm, Tool, or concrete model; the applied activity remains Method.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Technique, procedure, or applied approach used to perform part of the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude a single technique, a data description, or an illustrative example without evaluation.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Delimited empirical or computational test combining data, methods/models, conditions, and evaluation.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude evaluated experiments and incidental phrases introduced by 'for example'.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Single illustrative case, scenario, or application used to demonstrate an idea or procedure.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude goals, expectations, recommendations, and findings attributed only to cited work.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Empirical, computational, analytical, qualitative, negative, or null result produced by the current study.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Finding states what was observed; Discussion explains why it occurred or what it implies.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Atomic interpretation or explanation of a result.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude bare citations and bibliographic records; cited-Paper grounding is a separate protocol.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Substantive description, comparison, or synthesis of prior research.

targetDefinitions.boundary: ResearchProblem predates and motivates the study; FutureWork proposes a later action.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit constraint, weakness, uncertainty, or boundary of the current study, method, experiment, data, or finding.

targetDefinitions.boundary: A repeated metric or result is still a Finding unless the text performs a higher-level synthesis.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Study-level synthesis or general conclusion derived by the authors.

targetDefinitions.boundary: ResearchGoal is intended action; ResearchSignificance is why the contribution matters.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: What the study claims to have added to knowledge, evidence, method, infrastructure, or practice.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Exclude current-study goals, generic aspirations, and future actions of an experimental agent.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit future research activity proposed by the authors.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Do not infer a hypothesis from a question, objective, design, or expected result.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Explicit, testable proposition that the current study intends to evaluate.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Not every declarative sentence is a Claim; avoid duplicate Claim and Conclusion nodes for the same unit.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Argumentatively important proposition asserted by the authors but not necessarily a direct empirical result.

targetDefinitions.boundary: Preserve source-scoped identity and version wording; do not promote by name alone.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Dataset named or described in publication prose without sufficient exact identity for DatasetResource.

targetDefinitions.boundary: DatasetMention identifies a dataset; DataDescription explains its characteristics.
targetDefinitions.positive_criterion: Atomic description of data origin, period, coverage, sample, resolution, variables, partition, or composition.
